screening_results.reason: The study is task-based fMRI with 7 FTD patients and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with Talairach coordinates (meets I3, I5, I7, I8). However, it does not explicitly state that patients had behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) per inclusion criterion I4, and crucially it does not report between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space as required by I6; the reported contrasts are FTD vs AD. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (uncertain/specification of bvFTD) and I6 (no bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast).

This study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses (SPM) with whole-brain, group-level results in MNI space (e.g., coordinate 4,62,-6) comparing clinically diagnosed FTD patients to age-matched controls. The sample (n=29 FTD patients) excludes primary progressive aphasia and semantic dementia, and the clinical description (inappropriate social behavior, loss of insight) matches the behavioral variant phenotype. Control groups per center are reported (>=6 per center). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. All required imaging, sample size, between-group voxelwise contrasts, and whole-brain coordinate reporting criteria are met. No exclusion criteria (systematic review, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness-only, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Note: 3 patients had mild motor neuron signs, but the cohort is still clinically FTD and the paper treats a homogeneous FTD group rather than pooling with other dementia types.

The study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes, but it does not specifically investigate or report results for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as a distinct group. The FTD sample is heterogeneous (15 PPA variants; 14 with social/executive dysfunction) and all analyses are reported for the pooled FTD group versus controls; no bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails the requirement for inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients analyzed separately and fails the requirement for bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD-specific sample), I6 (bvFTD vs control contrast not reported), I7 (bvFTD-specific whole-brain result not provided). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study (I3) that includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and reports a NON-APH subgroup (non-aphasic, social/executive impairment) consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). The NON-APH subgroup has n=14 (meets sample size criterion I5) and imaging included a healthy control group (n=12). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group-level contrasts and correlations (normalized to Talairach coordinates) for FTD subgroups including NON-APH versus controls (I6, I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results and peak coordinates are presented in tables and figures (I8). Full text contains methods, results and tables/figures; no exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review as a VBM whole-brain study reporting bvFTD (NON-APH) results.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis: it uses FDG-PET (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed FTD patient group (25 patients) diagnosed per revised Lund-Manchester criteria consistent with behavioral-variant FTD clinical features (I4); has adequate sample sizes (25 patients, 15 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 (I5); reports voxel-wise whole-brain SPM99 analyses with stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space comparing the FTD group to controls (I6, I7) and provides the whole-brain results as clusters and peak coordinates in the text (I8). The paper presents full methods, results, and discussion, and separates FTD and semantic dementia groups (FTD results are not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Sample sizes meet thresholds (9 FTD, 26 controls). The analysis is voxelwise, whole-brain, and reports group-level between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and cluster results, satisfying requirements for reporting in a defined stochastic space. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not exclusively FC/DTI/cortical thickness; no evidence of comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia confounds). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and should be INCLUDED.

Sample size exceeds the minimum (patients=29; controls=11). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, figures, and tables.

The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). The report includes whole-brain, voxelwise results (figures and described contrasts). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reported voxelwise group comparisons (MAPT and GRN mutation groups vs. controls) in stereotactic space. The MAPT group (n=11) presented initially with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), and the GRN group (n=9) included bvFTD cases; healthy controls n=15. All patient groups meet the minimum sample size. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cross-sectional VBM and longitudinal voxel-wise analyses) clearly identified for the mutation groups (including the MAPT group that presented with bvFTD) and provides maps/analyses in MNI space. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not using only excluded modalities). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient for screening.

Decision: EXCLUDED. Rationale: The study uses FDG-PET imaging and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of an FTD group versus controls in Talairach space, with an adequate sample size (FTD n=13; controls n=26). However, the paper does not specify that the FTD sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, and the meta-analysis inclusion criterion I4 explicitly requires bvFTD or Pick's disease. Therefore it fails I4 and must be excluded. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast in Talairach space for the FTD group vs controls), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the FTD group), I8 (results presented/defined in text/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (clinical diagnosis specifically of bvFTD or Pick's disease not clearly reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study used task-based fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample size (bvFTD n=10 overall; imaging subset bvFTD n=7) meeting the sample-size criterion (I5), it does not report any whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The structural (VBM) imaging results reported in the paper combine bvFTD and PNFA into a single patient group for the between-group VBM contrasts, and the task fMRI was conducted only in healthy young adults. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-only whole-brain between-group results) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) subgroup characterized by behavioral/personality changes consistent with bvFTD (I4). This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (bvFTD) with matched controls. Imaging modality: FDG-PET (meets I3). Sample: 21 bvFTD patients (15 men, 6 women) and 30 controls (FDG-PET available for 12 controls) satisfying minimum sample size (meets I4 and I5). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses in standard space (MNI) including between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) and parametric voxelwise regressions within the bvFTD group relating hypometabolism to behavioral scores; results are reported with coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds (meets I6, I7, I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not a review and does not rely solely on ROIs or excluded modalities. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study fulfills all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) structural MRI volumetric analyses (Freesurfer-derived regional volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). This FDG-PET study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I5 (patient group n=14 and control group n=33, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (participants are pathologically confirmed FTLD and AD but not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD group), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text is complete. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its cohort (I4). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (42 patients, 30 controls) (I5). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast that is specifically and exclusively comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls; all whole-brain VBM results are reported for pathologically defined FTLD-TDP subtypes (types 1–3) rather than a bvFTD-only group. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups) and I7 (a whole-brain, voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=21) meeting the sample size requirement (I4, I5), it does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that directly compares bvFTD versus controls as an independent group-level result. The VBM results are reported as correlations of conjunction-search accuracy with gray matter across subjects and subsequent extracted-voxel ANOVAs comparing diagnostic groups, not as a primary whole-brain bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control contrast in stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses 18F-FDG PET) and I5 (patient group size ≥6; FTLD N=31). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Picks disease — sample is labeled FTLD without bvFTD-specific reporting), I6 (no between-group whole-brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) directly apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (SPM99) relating bvFTD patients to healthy controls, including two-sample t-tests and regression analyses linking IRI empathy scores to gray-matter atrophy. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (N=12) (I4) and imaging controls (N=12), satisfying sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts of bvFTD versus controls and voxelwise results with cluster thresholds and a results table/figure (Table 2, Figure 1) in standardized coordinates via SPM (I6, I7). Results are presented in tables/figures described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria apply; the study is empirical, not a review, includes whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), and excludes other dementia causes per methods. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients: 16 bvFTD cases within 26 FTLD patients), and I5 (patient n=26; control n=21). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls—the VBM analyses are within the combined FTLD cohort (and no MR images were acquired for controls). It also does NOT meet I7: there are whole-brain voxelwise results, but these are reported for the combined FTLD sample, not as a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

The study is excluded because it reports only lobar/ROI volumetry and group comparisons on region volumes rather than whole-brain, voxelwise stereotactic results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses automated voxel-based volumetry based on SPM5, analogous to VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTLD subgroup), I5 (bvFTLD N=6 and controls N=30). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTLD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified from the target sample), I8 (not applicable as no voxelwise tables/coordinates provided). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not provide the required stereotactic, whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/results and is excluded.

This is an empirical study that uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (with results reported in MNI standard space) to examine grey matter atrophy related to disinhibition in a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) sample. Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=14; controls n=18). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD) with tables and figures of coordinates and TFCE-corrected results; VBM findings are complemented by diffusion tensor imaging but VBM alone satisfies imaging modality inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, empirical data). Full text content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study is an open-label FDG-PET investigation in a mixed FTD sample and does not provide a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=7 ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the sample and for bvFTD subgroup), I8 (results reported with coordinates/MNI-Talairach). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space; only within-subject before-vs-after and subgroup SPM analyses without a healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded for the purposes of this meta-analysis focused on between-group bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrasts.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=21) and matched controls (I4, I5), and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-sample t tests) comparing bvFTD to controls assessed in standard space (MNI coordinates used for seeds and voxelwise analyses) with whole-brain, cluster-level corrected results (satisfying I6 and I7). Results are presented in figures and described in text (acceptable per I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disallowed comorbid sample, empirical original data, and not limited solely to excluded modalities). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5 (minimum sample size). Both bvFTD patient groups are N=5 (bvFTD(CBD)=5; bvFTD(Pick’s)=5), below the required >=6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD / Pick’s patients), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in SPM5 with coordinate-based results), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group results), I8 (reports results in tables/figures described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient group sizes <6). Exclusion criteria applicable: none (E5,E6,E7,E8,E9 not met). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxel-based morphometry (VBM) contrast comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls with stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick's disease cases), and I5 (sufficient overall MRI sample sizes: 42 patients, 35 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD clinical group versus controls in MNI/Talairach space — VBM results are presented by pathological subgroups, not bvFTD syndromic group) and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. The provided full text appears complete.

This empirical study includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses relating grey-matter atrophy to performance and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts for bvFTD vs. controls. The sample includes 14 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients overall and 8 bvFTD patients with MRI data (controls n=40), meeting the minimum sample sizes. The paper provides group-level whole-brain VBM results (SPM5) and regression analyses in stereotactic space, and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in stereotactic space (Criterion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size N=31 ≥6), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results within the bvFTD sample), and I8 (coordinates/MNI space reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclusion is based on failure to provide a between-group bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast (I6).

The study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) but does not provide results specific to clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. The FTLD subgroup includes only N=13 with FTD=3, which is likely too small and not clearly identified as bvFTD, so I4 not satisfied and I5 not satisfied (bvFTD-specific group <6). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls with the bvFTD group unpooled (I6 not satisfied). Although whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, these are not clearly identified as coming from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are clearly met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: exclude because target-sample-related inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are not met despite appropriate imaging modality (I3).

This is an FDG-PET whole-brain study (I3 satisfied) including a mixed cohort of early dementias with an FTLD subgroup. However, the paper does not provide data specific to behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD)/Pick’s disease at the group level: the FTLD subgroup includes only 3 patients labelled 'FTD' (n=3, <6), and reported group-level contrasts are for pooled FTLD (and AD) versus subjective cognitive impairment rather than a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s disease sample reported as target group), I5 (at least 6 patients in target patient group), I6 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts in standard space), and I7 (a whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD/bvFTD-only sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by this study. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires bvFTD-specific, group-level whole-brain coordinates with adequate sample size, this study is excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (11 bvFTD patients, 11 matched controls) meeting the minimum of 6 per group (I5); reports between-group voxelwise analyses comparing bvFTD to controls using voxel-wise two-sample t-tests (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (VBM) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7); and the whole-brain results are presented in figures/text (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded imaging modality). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of behavioural-variant FTD groups (C9ORF72, MAPT, GRN, sporadic bvFTD) versus controls and direct between-group contrasts. Clinical samples consist of bvFTD patients (all genetic groups and sporadic bvFTD) and a control group. Each patient group exceeds the minimum sample size (C9ORF72 n=19, MAPT n=25, GRN n=12, sporadic bvFTD n=20) and controls n=40. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (VBM with SPM5, family-wise error correction) and presented in figures/tables; thus group-level whole-brain evidence from the target bvFTD samples is available. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the study does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast specifically comparing bvFTD patients (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls. The study is excluded because it does not use an accepted imaging modality for this review (I3 not met) and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (I6/I7 not met). Instead, the paper reports region-of-interest cortical and subcortical volumetric correlations derived from Freesurfer parcellation (ROI-based structural volumetry), and no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps are provided. The study does satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, N=32) and I5 (patient group and control group sizes ≥6), and the full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) relating grey matter density to self-appraisal; includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=49) and healthy controls (n=30); reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts and regressions with peak coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls; provides full methods, results, and discussion in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3). The sample includes 13 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (part of the FTLD sample) and 19 controls, meeting the minimum group sizes (I4, I5). The paper presents whole-brain, voxel-wise group comparisons of bvFTD versus controls after spatial normalization to standard space (MNI) with statistical parametric maps and figures, satisfying between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space and whole-brain results (I6, I7, I8). The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and result-space criteria required by the review. This study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and does not report whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports region-based/volumetric analyses and individual deformation maps, but lacks whole-brain voxelwise results). This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study (also used VBM for gray-matter correction) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (8 bvFTD patients) and healthy controls (16). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM and ICA/seed-based methods, and results are reported with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., DLPFC peak at x=36,y=42,z=30), with direct bvFTD vs control contrasts and subgroup-specific findings. Sample sizes meet the minimum (>=6). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain results; does not report only ROI/DTI/seed-only analyses; participants without disqualifying comorbidities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space. The MRI/VBM analyses are correlations of grey matter with task performance conducted within the patient group (MRI available for 16 patients); controls did not contribute to whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls in MNI/Talairach space) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I7 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

While the study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: uses VBM; I4: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24); I5: patient group size >=6), it does NOT meet key criteria required for inclusion. It also does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) results that are specific to the bvFTD sample alone (I7 not met); the reported VBM analyses are regression/voxelwise correlations across a mixed patient cohort and the authors state analyses by individual patient groups produced no significant results. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain voxelwise results.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes 20 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, meeting I3, I4 and the sample-size requirement I5. However, it does not report any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6). Analyses were performed within a frontal mask rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (fails I7). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study uses VBM (I3) and has adequate group sizes (37 FTD patients, controls) meeting I5. However, the patient sample is a heterogeneous FTD group (only a small subset explicitly described as behavioural-variant FTD) and the analyses and reported results treat FTD as a pooled group rather than reporting results for a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD subgroup separately. The paper does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD-only group; results are reported mainly as ROI-wise classification accuracies rather than voxel-coordinate tables or explicit whole-brain maps for bvFTD. Therefore it fails I4 (bvFTD sample not isolated) and I6/I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise, stereotactic-coordinate results). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the reported results are effectively ROI-based without the required whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/maps for the target bvFTD group.

This is an empirical VBM study including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and controls (n=15), and reports voxelwise between-group results in MNI space; however, all VBM analyses were conducted within a prefrontal/striatal ROI mask rather than as whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample present), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6), I6 (between-group contrasts reported in MNI space for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result for the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only ROI-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I7 and meets E6.

Full text is complete. Imaging modalities satisfy I3 (VBM/MRI and FDG-PET used). Sample sizes satisfy I5 (FTLD n=11; controls n=13). However, the FTLD group is a pooled sample (FTD n=4, SD n=5, mixed n=2) and the paper does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts or coordinate results specifically for a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease group that are separate from other FTLD subtypes. Therefore I4 (explicit bvFTD/Pick’s group), I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls without pooling), and I7 (group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Because the target of the meta-analysis is bvFTD and this study does not provide isolated whole-brain results for a bvFTD-only group, it must be excluded.

Study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a sufficient number of FTD patients overall (I5). However, it does not specify that patients have behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). The paper reports multivariate classification and discriminative images but does not provide a between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This empirical study reports both task-based fMRI (healthy adults) and voxelwise structural MRI analyses in a bvFTD sample. Structural images (T1) were processed with ANTs/PipeDream to compute gray matter probability (VBM-like approach), and a two-sample voxelwise SPM8 analysis compared bvFTD patients to healthy seniors with FDR-corrected whole-brain clusters reported. MRI sample for volumetric analyses was N=11 bvFTD and N=14 controls (both >6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) in stereotactic space and presents results in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and comorbidities were excluded clinically). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and should be included.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) using voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI, reporting whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. Imaging modalities include VBM (structural) and task fMRI (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (initial N=11; N=8 included in neuroimaging analyses) and healthy controls (N=16 functional, N=48 for VBM) meeting the minimum group size (I4, I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results normalized to a standard space (MNI) with tables and figures of coordinates for atrophy and activation contrasts (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review/meta-analysis, reports whole-brain (not ROI-only) results, includes an appropriate clinical sample without pooling with other patient groups, and uses accepted imaging modalities. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates bvFTD (n=10) vs controls (n=10) and AD (n=10). Whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses were performed and group-level between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs Controls and bvFTD vs AD) are reported in MNI space; anatomical loci and networks are described. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study reporting voxelwise group analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) to healthy controls (n=19). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4) with adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with results in MNI space and tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables/figures described) is provided, permitting assessment of methods and outcomes (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review and is suitable for inclusion.

This study used FDG-PET (I3) and had adequate patient group sizes (I5: FTLD n=11, AD n=11, CVD n=9). However, it does not explicitly state that the FTLD group comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Critically, the imaging results are reported as regional ROI z-scores and qualitative regional hypometabolism (e.g., temporoparietal, bifrontal) rather than stereotactic, voxelwise whole-brain coordinates (no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise maps reported). Therefore the study does not provide the required between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space (I6/I7/I8 not met) and instead meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This VBM study meets I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the FTLD cohort), and I5 (sample size: 37 FTLD patients, bvFTD subgroup >6). However it does NOT meet I6 or I7: the reported voxelwise contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups (and include syndromic group as a covariate) rather than presenting any between-group contrast of bvFTD versus healthy controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported, they are not clearly identified as originating from a bvFTD-vs-control comparison. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide the required bvFTD-to-control voxelwise whole-brain contrast (I6, I7 not met).

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD among 40 FTD patients) (I4) and has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=18; controls n=27) (I5). The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results reported in MNI coordinates (e.g., x=8,y=28,z=-28) and FWE-corrected group atrophy maps (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain results (E5, E6, E8, E9 not applicable; no evidence of disallowed comorbid samples per text)

This paper is a study protocol/description of an ongoing observational cohort (LOF study). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET is included as an imaging modality in the protocol). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are recruited based on late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms, not a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (no reported bvFTD patient group size ≥6 is presented; the paper reports planned total cohort and expected FTD cases but no confirmed bvFTD group), I6 (no between-group voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates or contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported), I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). The manuscript lacks empirical group-level neuroimaging results required by the review (coordinates/voxelwise contrasts) and therefore must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (11 bvFTD participants) and healthy controls (15). Voxel-based morphometry was used and whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (patient subgroups vs controls) and voxelwise correlations are reported and overlaid in MNI space; results (including cluster-level findings and figures/tables) are described in main text and supplementary materials. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 participant requirement for patient and control groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results attributable specifically to the bvFTD group (bvFTD vs controls) and provides coordinates/overlays in MNI space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analyses, non-empirical, irrelevant imaging modality, disallowed patient comorbidities) are violated. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging analyses) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study (with complementary VBM) of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) compared to age- and sex-matched controls (n=19). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts using FSL randomize with TFCE and presents MNI coordinates and figures/tables of results. All required inclusion criteria are met (imaging modality: rfMRI/VBM; clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; sample sizes ≥6 in both groups; between-group contrasts in standard space; whole-brain voxelwise group-level results clearly attributed to the bvFTD group). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed modality) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

Although this study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD cases; I4) with adequate patient group size (n=32; I5), and reports voxelwise coordinates/cluster results (I8), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (i.e., no bvFTD-specific group vs control whole-brain contrast). The reported analyses are correlational (Reserve Index vs connectivity) within a mixed FTD sample and GRN+/- subgroups, and difference-of-slope comparisons between genetic subgroups, rather than a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study should be excluded because it reports ROI-based diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) results rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses required by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study uses only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (study reports DTI rather than allowed modalities). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6: 8 bvFTD, 12 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is DTI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the modality and whole-brain voxelwise requirements and must be excluded.

Although this study includes VBM analyses (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate group size (n=48; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain VBM results (I7) described in text/figures (I8), it does not present a whole-brain between-group imaging contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group to healthy controls. The reported VBM contrasts are primarily AD versus bvFTD (patient vs patient), and the imaging cohort lacks a concurrent healthy control imaging comparison for bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (bvFTD vs controls imaging contrast in MNI/Talairach space) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its sample, and has sufficient total patient (n=15) and control (n=12) group sizes. However, the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts that isolate a bvFTD-only group versus controls in MNI or Talairach space. Reported whole-brain VBM results are for the combined FTD group versus controls and for FTD subgroupings (fast vs slow acquisition), but bvFTD is not analyzed or reported separately. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 required for inclusion in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study (FSL–VBM in MNI space) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=18) and age/education-matched healthy controls (n=28). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (including covariate analyses and group comparisons) with results clearly identified for the bvFTD group (e.g., VBM correlations of IGT modified net score within bvFTD). Imaging methods specify MNI152 registration. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core data appear complete. Therefore the study meets the imaging modality (VBM), target diagnosis (bvFTD), sample size thresholds, and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space.

The study examines FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) but does not specify that patients were diagnosed with the behavioral variant (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; thus inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Although the paper uses voxel-wise FDG‑PET and MRI analyses (I3 satisfied), appears to have adequate group sizes for analyses (I5 satisfied), and reports whole-brain results in maps/tables (I8 satisfied), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick’s) group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (both sporadic bvFTD and C9ORF72 mutation carriers), and reports adequate sample sizes (sporadic bvFTD n=15; C9 n=8; Controls n=15). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (each patient group vs. controls) with results referenced to MNI space and detailed voxelwise analyses (permutation testing, cluster results, and anatomical labeling). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, prohibited imaging modalities, or comorbid samples) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and directly compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) to healthy controls (n=18) using whole-brain, voxelwise analyses normalized to MNI space. It reports group contrasts (controls>FTD, FTD>PSP, etc.) and voxelwise correlation results, with results described in the text and figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The sample sizes exceed the minimum, and there is no evidence of excluded comorbid psychiatric or other-dementia confounds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because, although it uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=6), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls. Analyses were performed using region-of-interest (ROI) measures and visual inspection; no coordinates or voxelwise group-level results are provided, and there is no control group comparison presented for bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (bvFTD group size = 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis: (1) Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). (2) Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=10) (I4). (3) Sample sizes: bvFTD group (n=10) and control group (n=14) both ≥6 (I5). (4) Between-group contrasts: VBM t-tests comparing bvFTD to controls were reported (I6). (5) Whole-brain evidence: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the bvFTD group (I7). (6) Results reported in standard space: MNI coordinates and tables/figures are provided (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited modalities). Full text appears complete (methods, results, VBM tables/figures, discussion). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it performed a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) according to consensus criteria (I4) with adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=22; controls n=34) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5). The VBM was conducted in standard space (registration to MNI template) and patient-control voxelwise comparisons were reported (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with TFCE and permutation testing), with bvFTD vs. controls contrasts described and results provided in supplementary figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical data, not limited to excluded modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and acknowledgements present).

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets I3, I4) with sufficient sample size (15 bvFTD/fd+ cases; meets I5). However, it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it provide coordinate tables or group-level voxelwise results (fails I6 and I7). The imaging results are presented as qualitative reads and diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity), not as voxelwise group contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain results / only non-coordinate qualitative imaging) and does not satisfy required inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 satisfied), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=28) (I4 satisfied), and meets sample size requirements for patients and controls (I5 satisfied), it does not report any whole-brain, group-level between-group VBM contrasts that directly compare the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The imaging results are voxelwise correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample (polisher/tarnisher subsamples and whole-sample correlations) rather than a bvFTD-versus-control group contrast; therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none.
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (bvFTD group n=11 ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM results for the bvFTD group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text).
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is tensor-based morphometry [TBM], not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no comparison of bvFTD group to healthy controls; between-group contrasts are bvFTD vs early-onset AD, not controls).

Conclusion: Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, adequate sample size, and reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM analyses, it does not meet modality requirements (I3) nor provide the required bvFTD vs healthy-control whole-brain contrasts (I6) required for inclusion in this meta-analysis, so it must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The paper reports within-group VBM regression analyses correlating reward-seeking scores in a bvFTD-only sample (group-level voxelwise results), not a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients), I5 (patient sample n=91 for imaging analyses, ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample), I8 (results reported in MNI coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used VBM (I3), included adequate group sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I7,I8). However, the sample comprises heterogeneous FTD phenotypes (GRN+ and GRN- FTD) rather than a clearly defined bvFTD (behavioural-variant FTD) group, and no between-group contrast is reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls. Therefore it does not meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease) nor I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls). Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=46), and reports whole-brain VBM results in tables/figures. However, it does not report a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI or Talairach space. The imaging analyses are primarily correlational across a mixed diagnostic sample (and analyses of ‘overestimators’/‘underestimators’), and although diagnostic group membership was used as a covariate in some analyses, no clear bvFTD vs. control whole-brain group-level contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise results (MNI space) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The paper used voxel-based morphometry (VBM), included 13 bvFTD patients and 12 controls (both >6), and reports between-group contrasts and coordinates (MNI) for bvFTD vs controls; group-level whole-brain results and figures/tables are presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not an excluded imaging modality). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study that directly investigates cerebellar grey matter in bvFTD and related groups. It meets inclusion criteria: uses VBM (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=23) (I4); has adequate sample sizes for bvFTD and controls (23 bvFTD, 16 controls) (I5); reports between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus controls registered to MNI space with voxelwise, whole-brain results (FWE-corrected) (I6, I7); and presents results in figures/text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria were triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/thickness-only, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbid sample characteristics).

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (7 bvFTD cases within the sample; meets I4), and has adequate group sizes (patient subgroup n=7 and controls n≥6; meets I5). However, all reported voxelwise whole-brain analyses are performed on the pooled FTD-GRN+ group (14 FTD-GRN+ comprising 7 bvFTD + 7 avPPA) versus controls. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that isolates the bvFTD subgroup alone compared to controls, nor coordinate-based/binary results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only group. Therefore it fails I6 and I7, which require bvFTD-specific, whole-brain between-group voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded for not providing bvFTD-specific whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses MRI-based morphometry/ VBM/TBM), I5 (FTD patient group size = 30, control group size ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise statistical parametric maps comparing patient group to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease — the paper refers generically to 'FTD' without specifying subtype), I6 (does not report between-group contrast coordinates in a standard stereotactic space such as MNI or Talairach; analyses are performed in a group-wise template space and SPM figures are described but stereotactic coordinates/tables in MNI/Talairach are not provided). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion IDs). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, full-text study that uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting‑state) functional MRI (I3). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets Neary and FTDC criteria) including C9orf72+ and C9orf72− groups (I4). Patient group sizes (14 and 14; total n=28) and control groups (HC1 n=42 for VBM; HC2 n=14 for fMRI) exceed the minimum of 6 participants (I5). The paper reports multiple between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., C9orf72+ < HC, C9orf72− < HC, and direct patient-group comparisons) using SPM8 with MNI normalization and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), it includes whole-brain results not only ROI analyses (E6), the sample is bvFTD (comorbid MND cases are within the bvFTD spectrum and do not constitute excluded disorders per E7), it is empirical original data (not E8), and it reports VBM and seed-based FC alongside whole‑brain analyses (E9 not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and DTI) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs Controls) with MNI coordinates and thresholded VBM results (tfce, FWE-corrected) as well as tract-based spatial statistics for DTI. Results for the bvFTD group are reported separately (not pooled) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise findings are clearly presented in text/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text is complete and shows the study used whole-brain VBM (satisfies I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (47 bvFTD; satisfies I4), and had adequate sample sizes (96 patients, 34 controls; satisfies I5). However, the paper’s neuroimaging results are within-patient correlational VBM analyses (atrophy correlated with happiness behavior) performed on the combined FTD sample and do not present a between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it does not meet I6 (no reported between-group bvFTD vs control contrast) nor I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Based on these missing inclusion criteria, the study should be excluded for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study that (1) uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (meets I3); (2) includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=18) (meets I4 and I5) with healthy controls (n=18); (3) reports between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (controls > bvFTD) with anatomical results reported in MNI space and figures/tables (meets I6, I7, I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, VBM processing), Results (group comparisons and correlations) and Discussion, so core article content is present (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported, and imaging modality is VBM rather than excluded modalities). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study used voxel-wise gray matter analyses (VBM-style preprocessing and voxelwise permutation tests in FSL) and reports group comparisons of GM density between clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and healthy controls in MNI space. Sample size meets thresholds (12 bvFTD patients, 14 healthy seniors; imaging available for 9 patients with an independent control imaging group of 35), and the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and regression analyses relating behavioral performance to regional GM atrophy (clusters reported and whole-brain regression in supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-FC/DTI/thickness-only, and no indication of excluded comorbid psychiatric/neurologic confounds). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is suitable for inclusion.

The study uses FDG-PET and VBM and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes, but the primary whole-brain voxel-wise analyses compare MAPT mutation carriers (a group combining symptomatic bvFTD and asymptomatic carriers) to non-carriers. The paper does not report a whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level contrast that is exclusively between a clinically-defined bvFTD (symptomatic) group and controls; voxelwise comparisons among symptomatic carriers alone were not performed due to small AC sample and group-level contrasts by diagnostic subgroup were limited to ROI/z-score analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and healthy controls (n=11). It uses fMRI as the imaging modality, reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls, and specifies analyses in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE whole-brain and small-volume corrected contrasts). All required inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental absence is acceptable.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13) (I4) and healthy controls (n=11), meeting the sample size threshold (I5); reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with voxelwise results and anatomical clusters (MNI stereotaxic reporting is indicated) (I6); and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified for the bvFTD sample (I7). Reporting of coordinates and cluster-level results (and figures/tables) satisfies I8. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain VBM results are explicitly described. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain, voxelwise analysis including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=14) and healthy controls (n=28). Between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) are reported and displayed in MNI space with voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected), satisfying group-level whole-brain results. Sample sizes for patient and control groups exceed the minimum of 6. The paper uses VBM (I3), includes bvFTD patients (I4), meets sample size requirements (I5), reports between-group MNI-space contrasts specific to bvFTD (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise results for the target group (I7), and presents results in figures/tables/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

While this study meets several inclusion criteria (uses voxel-based morphometry [I3], includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants [I4], and has adequate sample sizes in patient and control groups [I5]), it does NOT report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The main VBM analyses relate to (a) presence of ‘disgusting behaviors’ across a heterogeneous patient sample and (b) ROI analyses restricted to the insula within bvFTD/svPPA. There is no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming specifically from a bvFTD vs control contrast, so criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used FDG-PET (I3) and included a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD group (n=12) (I4) and a control group (n=10), meeting the minimum sample sizes (I5). The methods describe voxel-wise between-group contrasts registered to MNI space and report group-level whole-brain results comparing FTD to controls (voxel-wise analyses, MNI coordinates reported in Supplementary Table), satisfying I6 and I7. Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables as described (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=23); reports group-level VBM contrasts between each patient group (including bvFTD) and controls in MNI standard space and identifies significant clusters (whole-brain results). The paper provides methods registering to MNI space and reports region coordinates for imaging correlations. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) with an adequate control group (n=9), the imaging results are reported for a pooled FTD spectrum group (n=33) rather than for the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup alone. The meta-analysis requires group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts derived specifically from the bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group that are not pooled with other patient subtypes. This study therefore fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD-specific between-group contrast reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=22), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space; VBM analyses are within patient cohorts relating symptoms to grey matter, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control comparison). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used VBM and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=21), satisfying imaging and sample-size criteria. However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM analyses reported are correlation/regression analyses within the patient cohort and within the bvFTD subgroup (behaviour–anatomy correlations), not bvFTD versus control voxelwise group contrasts; whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed but yielded no significant between-group results. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 (no between-group bvFTD vs control contrast in stereotactic space) and I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as from the bvFTD group).

This full text meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (12 patients) and healthy controls (20) (I4, I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses registered to MNI space with group contrasts between bvFTD and controls (I6, I7), and results are presented in the main text/figures (I8). The paper is empirical, not a review, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only reporting, no seed-based FC/DTI-only methods, no psychiatric comorbidity exclusions). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM), Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore include.

This study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3) and reports only ROI-based volumetric and shape analyses of the caudate and putamen without whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). Exclusion criterion E6 applies (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). Sample includes an autopsy-confirmed/biomarker-negative behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=59) (I4) with matched healthy controls (n=61), satisfying sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to controls (adjusted voxel-wise VBM contrasts, p-values, and coordinate tables referenced in Supplementary Table 1), providing results in standard stereotactic space (coordinates) (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary materials (I8). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria required by the review. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=36) satisfying I4 and meets the minimum patient sample size (I5), it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — imaging used was structural MRI/CT and PET/SPECT without indication of FDG-PET (I3 not met). Crucially, the paper presents no between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls, and there is no healthy control group or whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6 and I7 not met; I8 therefore not applicable). No exclusion criteria are specifically triggered by the study content. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (11 patients) (I4) and a healthy control group (14) with both groups ≥6 participants (I5). It reports voxel-based morphometry whole-brain results (voxelwise atrophy in bvFTD) and uses MNI coordinates for voxelwise analyses, with between-group contrasts of bvFTD vs controls reported in main text and/or supplemental materials (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is available but not required. Hence include.

Full text reports VBM (voxel-based morphometry) analyses alongside DTI, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) and healthy controls (n=37), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and disease maps (bvFTD vs controls) using standard stereotactic analysis and permutation testing. Whole-brain VBM results are presented and summarized (with clusters/peaks referenced in figures/tables/supplementary material). The full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete and satisfies all required inclusion criteria without triggering any exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. It uses manual ROI-based hypothalamic volumetry on structural MRI (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and reports ROI results rather than whole-brain, voxelwise coordinates in a standard space. Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I3, I6, I7, and I8 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does satisfy I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD n=19; controls n=23). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the bvFTD-specific and whole-brain result criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM/tissue segmentation and VBM8 pipeline) and I5 (FTD patient group N=12 and controls N=18, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (FTD cases are reported without distinguishing subtypes — bvFTD or Pick's disease is not explicitly identified), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for a target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) (I4) and healthy controls (n=17), meeting the minimum sample sizes (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in MNI space (voxel-wise GLM, permutation tests, p<0.001 uncorrected, cluster extent threshold) and presents atrophy patterns and coordinates/figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and neuroimaging analyses, and no exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed imaging modality, and sample exclusions for psychiatric/substance histories were applied). Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD; n=31), and I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n=75). However, the neuroimaging analyses are covariate-based voxelwise regressions of BIS/BAS across the combined sample and co-atrophy checks; the paper does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) nor any bvFTD-specific whole-brain group-level voxelwise result. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to be met. Exclude on the basis of missing I6 and I7.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD subgroup (n=21) meeting the minimum patient group size (I4, I5). However, the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast (in MNI/Talairach space) that compares bvFTD alone to healthy controls with whole-brain group-level voxelwise results clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample (I6 and I7 are not satisfied based on the provided full text). Although VBM analyses and comparisons to healthy controls are referenced (some results said to be in Supplementary material), no explicit coordinates or whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are presented in the available full text. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) appear to apply. Therefore the study cannot be included for this meta-analysis because it fails to meet the required between-group, whole-brain reporting requirements (I6 and I7).

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (methods describe FSLVBM, registration to MNI152, and corrected voxelwise results presented as clusters/figures). Participants were clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (possible/probable/definite) with N=58 patients and comparisons to control subjects are reported (neuropsychological and imaging contrasts vs controls). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space (figures and supplemental tables referenced). Therefore it satisfies imaging modality (I3), clinical sample of bvFTD (I4), sufficient patient sample and reported control comparisons (I5), between-group contrasts in a defined space (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I7), and acceptable reporting of results in figures/tables/supplement (I8). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are met based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete for methods, results, and discussion.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (22 patients) and age-matched controls (22) satisfying sample-size requirements (I4, I5), and reports between-group voxelwise contrasts after registration to MNI space (I6). However, the neuroimaging analyses were conducted within a predefined fronto-subcortical region-of-interest mask rather than as an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analysis. The paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample; therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7). Because the study reports only ROI-restricted voxelwise results, it falls under the exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Conclusion: EXCLUDED (meets E6; satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6; does not satisfy I7).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has adequate sample sizes (24 bvFTD patients, 179 controls; I5), and reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (I6). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (interaction and group contrasts) clearly in the text and supplementary material (I7,I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review, ROI-only, DTI, cortical thickness-only, or seed-based FC study), and there is no indication of disqualifying comorbid samples. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references). Therefore, include for the meta-analysis of bvFTD VBM studies.

This is an empirical FDG-PET SPM study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=17), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses (single-subject comparisons to a normative FDG-PET database and group-level SPM results overlaid on an MNI template) and presents group-level voxelwise findings linking hypometabolism to socio-emotional deficits. These analyses constitute between-group contrasts against a normative control database and provide whole-brain results in stereotactic space, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review paper, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, or comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds) are met.
