Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and satisfies the reporting allowance I8.

Exclusion reason: E6 (only ROI/ no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM, rs-fMRI, and FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=11), I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; study focuses on classification among patient groups rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported as coming from bvFTD vs controls). The full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls.

This is an empirical, two-center MRI study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons in MNI space. It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) and healthy controls (n=37), meeting the minimum sample size. The paper presents group-level whole-brain VBM and TBSS (DTI) results for bvFTD versus controls and bvFTD versus AD, with voxelwise statistical results and describes ROIs derived from those voxelwise contrasts; results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review/meta-analysis only, ROI-only, non-empirical, or exclusive use of disallowed modalities) are met.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 patients) and matched healthy controls (30). Imaging modalities include resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Sample sizes exceed the required minimum (≥6 per group). The paper reports group-level between-group contrasts and voxelwise analyses with images normalized to MNI space and FDR-corrected whole-brain results (GM density differences, resting-state component maps and spectral/FNC comparisons), clearly identified as arising from the bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and comorbidities were excluded per methods). Full text is complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinate reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included) and I5 (patient group sizes: bvFTD n=14, AD n=19). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET as the primary imaging modality for reported results—main analyses used FreeSurfer volumetry and DTI), I6 (no between-group results reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria applicable: E9 (study reports DTI and cortical/volumetric measures rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET) and E6 (analyses are ROI-based with no whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=23) and healthy controls (n=50). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (images normalized to MNI space) with group-level contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and ROI insula analyses; results and correlations are reported. The study meets imaging modality (VBM), sample (bvFTD present), minimum sample sizes, reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space, and provides whole-brain group-level results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain results, no disallowed modality or pooling). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral-variant cases) and uses FDG-PET in a subset, it does not meet key imaging meta-analysis requirements. The paper presents descriptive imaging of a very small number of TBK1 carriers (FDG-PET in 2 patients; only five behavioral-variant FTD cases overall), and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. There is no voxelwise statistical comparison or coordinate table for a bvFTD vs control contrast, nor a sufficiently large bvFTD patient group for meta-analytic inclusion. Therefore it fails I5 (sample size), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group result). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the study provides no whole-brain voxelwise results (only individual/descriptive imaging findings). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons involving a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group versus healthy controls. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) with results reported in MNI stereotaxic space and cluster tables. Sample: 12 bvFTD patients and 12 controls (both ≥6). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for bvFTD relative to controls (TFCE, FWE-corrected p<0.05) and coordinates/cluster tables. Full article content (intro, methods, VBM results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and participants with comorbid psychiatric/substance diagnoses were excluded). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=26) compared to healthy controls (n=23). The paper uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry normalized to MNI space and reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (cluster-level FWE-corrected results and specific atrophy clusters) and regression analyses relating GM volume to behavioral measures. All required sample sizes are met and bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. The provided full text includes introduction, methods (VBM and behavioral), results (VBM group contrast and regressions), and discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because, although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes frontotemporal lobar degeneration patients with a behavioral-variant subgroup (35 bvFTD patients) satisfying the bvFTD sample requirement (I4) and has adequate patient and control group sizes (I5), it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in a standard stereotactic space specific to the bvFTD subgroup. Analyses are based on region-of-interest/parcellation (AAL VOIs) and metabolic connectivity patterns rather than voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinate contrasts; the FTLD analyses are reported at the group (FTLD) level rather than separately for bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This is an empirical VBM study (FSL-VBM) that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=25). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and between-group contrasts versus controls with results provided in stereotactic (MNI) space (clusters and coordinates reported in Table 3 and supplement). It also reports bvFTD-specific whole-brain covariate analyses correlating caloric intake with gray matter atrophy (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective of bvFTD imaging studies.

Although the study uses VBM and resting-state fMRI and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases with adequate sample sizes, the analyses combine bvFTD and avPPA into a single FTD-GRN+ group and do not report any voxelwise between-group contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts reported). Full text appears complete.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it employs voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients using Rascovsky criteria (I4), has ≥6 patients and controls (15 each) (I5), reports voxelwise between-group SPM analyses normalized to standard space allowing BV-FTD vs control contrasts (I6), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7/I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext is complete.

Exclusion criteria met: E6. This study used VBM (I3 satisfied) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 satisfied) with sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20; I5 satisfied). However, the VBM analyses reported in the paper are correlations within the combined patient cohort and significant findings are reported only within pre-specified regional volumes of interest (ROI-level, FWE-corrected within ROIs). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group alone versus controls, nor any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributable to the bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (only ROI results/no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise result). Full text appears complete and sufficient for assessment (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=33) and healthy controls (n=34). The paper reports voxel-based morphometry whole-brain group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (two-sample t-tests) with results reported in standard space (MNI) and peak coordinates (see Tables/Figures). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (cerebrum VBM with FWE-corrected thresholds), and additional seed coordinates and SUIT cerebellar analyses are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) (I4) and healthy controls (n=38) with sample sizes ≥6 (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results localized in MNI space (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7). Results and coordinates are reported in main text and supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports a voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM8 analysis comparing 25 bvFTD patients to 20 healthy controls using FDG-PET and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1 MRI. Imaging coordinates were reported and converted to Talairach space; between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) are presented in tables and figures. Sample size exceeds minimums. The patient sample comprises clinically diagnosed late-onset probable bvFTD (images acquired during a predementia stage but patients were selected as probable bvFTD), and results are not pooled with other patient groups. The study provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in standard space. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3), has adequate group sizes (bvFTD n=25; controls n=37) (I5), and reports between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI stereotaxic space (I6). However, the analyses were performed using an ROI mask focused on motor-system regions (methods state an ROI mask was created and ROI analyses conducted), and the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result for the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Hence the study is excluded.

The study is EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry/structural MRI VBM analyses) and I5 (patient group FTLD n=55 and controls n=73, both >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease; cases are pathologically defined FTLD subtypes without clear clinical bvFTD grouping), I6 and I7 (the paper does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Therefore the study does not meet the review requirement of reporting whole-brain voxelwise results for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and is excluded.

This is an empirical study that performs voxel-wise grey matter analyses (GMP images processed in ANTs/SPM8) consistent with VBM methods, reporting whole-brain voxelwise results normalized to MNI space. The sample includes 18 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 18 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and regression analyses relating atrophy to behavioral measures, with results presented as whole-brain analyses and figures/tables (coordinates/regions referenced). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (imaging and participants), Results (cognitive and imaging), and Discussion, so full text is complete. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because the imaging modality is surface-based cortical thickness and volumetric segmentation using FreeSurfer rather than VBM, FDG-PET, or fMRI (thus failing I3). It meets inclusion criteria I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD sample n=37 and controls n=33, both >6), and I7 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses). It does not meet I3 (required imaging modalities) and does not appear to provide between-group results in a standard stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) for voxelwise contrasts (I6 not met). Exclusion criterion E9 applies (study reports cortical thickness methods rather than accepted modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinical bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and a healthy control group (n=32). The authors performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses (SPM8) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of each clinical phenotype versus controls (see Supplementary Figure 1) as well as whole-brain correlations of clinical scales within the bvFTD group. Imaging modality (VBM), adequate sample sizes, and whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD subgroup satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia cases were excluded per methods). Although coordinate tables are not shown in the supplied text, results are reported in figures/supplementary material and described in the text, which is acceptable under the protocol.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria required by the review. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (the study reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain/voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 requirement: bvFTD n=11, controls n=20). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study uses structural ROI analyses and ASL perfusion, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in standard stereotactic space with MNI/Talairach coordinates for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete; exclusion is based on methodological and reporting criteria.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses reporting group-level contrasts and MNI coordinates, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) and healthy controls (n=20), and reports between-group voxelwise comparisons (bvFTD vs Controls) with whole-brain results presented as clusters/coordinates. The full text includes methods, results, and VBM tables/figures. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not use any of the eligible imaging modalities (I3). It uses diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion, and structural MRI (GM volume), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present; n=9) and I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). The paper also reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBSS) comparing bvFTD with controls, satisfying I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality) and I6 (study does not clearly report between-group results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] in the provided text; no coordinate table or coordinates are present). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails the modality eligibility (I3).

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group contrasts and voxelwise covariate analyses with MNI coordinates comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The bvFTD sample (n=24) and control sample (n=22) both exceed the minimum size. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (bvFTD vs Controls) are reported (tables/figures) and anatomical coordinates are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed imaging modality). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=23) and a healthy control group (N=20), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results (two-sample t-test comparing bvFTD to controls) and voxelwise regression analyses linking behavioral measures to GM volume. The paper provides whole-brain results (group comparison and regressions) that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample and refers to figures/tables/supplementary materials for results/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), does not use only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and there is no indication of disqualifying comorbid psychiatric/substance/other-dementia samples. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and imaging details; supplementary tables are referenced. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for a bvFTD imaging meta-analysis: it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=54) (I4) and healthy controls (n=27–43 depending on analyses) with sample sizes above the minimum (I5). The imaging approach includes whole-brain, voxelwise gray-matter analyses using volumetric T1 data and permutation-based Randomise testing (voxelwise GM atrophy and regression analyses), which is consistent with VBM-style whole-brain analyses (I3). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts for each patient group (including bvFTD vs. controls) (I6, I7), and these whole-brain results are described in the text and referenced in tables/figures/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not a review, not ROI-only, excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementia cases). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus, include.

Exclusion based on lack of whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise/MNI or Talairach coordinate results comparing bvFTD to controls; assessments were visual ratings and diagnostic accuracy metrics), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for decision-making.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=90 with MRI) with age-matched controls (n=44). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM/VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (VBM T-maps, family-wise error corrected) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls (Figure 2B; methods state SPM8 normalization implying MNI space). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (both patient and control groups ≥6). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in the text; thus results are available in a defined stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-FC/DTI-only, non-empirical) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (ICA/dual regression) as an imaging modality (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=12) (I4) with matched healthy controls (n=17) and patient group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (Randomize/TBSS) with between-group contrasts including bvFTD vs controls (not pooled with other diagnoses) and refers to cluster/ supplement tables for results (I6, I7, I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for coordinates/cluster information. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and the sample exclusions reported mean comorbid psychiatric/neurological/substance cases were excluded). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of 52 patients who met Rascovsky criteria for probable bvFTD, using voxel-wise SPM analyses at single-subject and group levels compared to a normal image database (n=112). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-tests and conjunction analyses with proper SPM normalization (template-based) and FWE-corrected thresholds, clearly identifying frontal and temporo-limbic metabolic patterns and associated neuropsychological correlations. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I8 (results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state and task-based fMRI; VBM and voxelwise resting-state group comparisons are reported. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for patients and controls. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (VBM comparison of bvFTD vs controls; resting-state connectivity differences) with peak coordinates provided (e.g., left ATL [−45,13,−37], left IFG [−52,2,14]), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly described. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Figures, coordinates) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disqualifying comorbid sample; not non-empirical; not limited to seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness only). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: (I3) uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) for neural atrophy analyses; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (34 meeting revised bvFTD criteria); (I5) sample sizes exceed thresholds (bvFTD patients n=34; control group n=30; subgroup sizes AbvFTD n=18, DbvFTD n=16); (I6) reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls (AbvFTD vs Controls, DbvFTD vs Controls) in stereotactic voxelwise analyses (SPM/VBM pipeline; Supplementary Table/Figures reported); (I7) provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FDR-corrected VBM results reported); (I8) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text (supplementary tables/figures referenced). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met: the study is empirical, not a review; reports whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only); patient sample was clinically defined without reported disqualifying comorbidities; and imaging modality is VBM (not solely seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD group of n=15), and I5 (bvFTD n=15 and controls n=15). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported VBM analyses are (a) a comparison of a mixed ‘poor melody score’ patient subgroup (patients with mixed diagnoses) vs controls and (b) covariate/correlation analyses across all patients merged together. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied (no bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast reported), so the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (and VBM) as imaging modalities (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (probable bvFTD) (I4) with n=12 and a control group (n=22), satisfying minimum sample sizes (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls using whole-brain voxel-based analyses (dual regression, voxel-wise nonparametric permutation testing with TFCE and FWE correction) and refers to coordinate tables/figures (Table 2/figures), meeting I6–I8. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample issues reported). Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is an empirical multimodal imaging paper that meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=26) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=22) with sample sizes ≥6 (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) with whole-brain VBM results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and describes these group-level, whole-brain voxelwise findings in the text/figures/supplementary material (I6,I7,I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), not ROI-only (E6), clinical sample exclusions were applied to avoid comorbid psychiatric/other dementias (so E7 not met), it is empirical (E8 not met), and it does not only report seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness (E9 not met). Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an original empirical study that directly compares FDG-PET (and ASL-MRI) measures in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample versus AD and cognitively normal controls. It reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level analyses (PLS logistic regression and voxel-wise GLMs with FDR correction) and presents spatial maps/figures separating bvFTD from controls and from AD. Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=32; CN n=15). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper is a study protocol (no original empirical results). Exclusion E8 applies: non-empirical paper without original data. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (protocol includes resting-state BOLD fMRI), I4 (recruits FTD syndromes using Rascovsky criteria, which target bvFTD), I5 (plans to recruit ≥16 participants per diagnostic group). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the manuscript contains no between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results (no coordinates/MNI/Talairach contrasts) comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it cannot contribute coordinate-based whole-brain data required by the review. Full text appears complete (protocol with methods) but lacks results. Exclusion applied: E8.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (methods and MNI coordinates reported) to examine grey-matter correlates of psychosis in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort (bvFTD and bvFTD-ALS). Sample sizes meet thresholds (56 patients, 23 controls). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and whole-brain, group-level results in MNI space (permutation-based GLM, FWE-corrected and uncorrected cluster results, with supplementary coordinate tables). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary tables/figures noted. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not solely other imaging modalities or non-empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (Lund and Manchester criteria; n=21) and healthy controls (n=25), satisfying sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group ICA and dual regression) comparing bvFTD to controls with voxelwise inference (permutation testing, TFCE) and refers to MNI coordinates for results (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/thickness only). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

Although this study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=58) with sufficient sample sizes and healthy controls (n=44), it does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls. The VBM results are presented as brain–behavior correlations across a mixed sample of NDG patients and controls (and coatrophy checks parameterized diagnostic groups), rather than group-level voxelwise bvFTD vs. control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain analyses (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) (I4) and matched healthy controls (n=22) with sample sizes >6 (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls, with images normalized to MNI space and whole-brain, voxelwise results reported (FWE-corrected) (I6,I7). Results are presented in the text and described as whole-brain voxelwise findings (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not restricted to excluded modalities, and sample is appropriate). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses FDG-PET imaging (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=26) (I4) with healthy controls (n=24) and AD group; all groups exceed the ≥6-participant minimum (I5). The authors performed voxel-wise whole-brain analyses using SPM8 with spatial normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template (MNI), and report between-group voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls and subgroup contrasts) with coordinate/cluster results (Supplementary Tables and SPM maps) (I6, I7, I8). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study examines presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), so it does not meet the requirement that the sample include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients (I4). It therefore also fails the meta-analysis requirement to report between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6). The paper does meet several methodological criteria: it uses VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3), includes adequate sample sizes (preSxC9 n=15; controls >6) (I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), and reports results in acceptable formats (I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I4 and I6 are not satisfied.

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI space, with sufficient sample sizes (52 patients, 52 controls). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. The VBM methods and voxelwise results (FWE-corrected) and SVM classification based on the VBM data are described. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for this review (VBM modality, clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, ≥6 participants per group, between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space, and reporting of whole-brain group-level results). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=16) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs. healthy controls) in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) specific to the bvFTD group. The VBM analyses reported are brain–behavior correlations across the entire mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy-adjusted maps, not group-level bvFTD vs. control contrasts; no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in the main text (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level between-group whole-brain result for the target sample. No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an empirical, voxelwise longitudinal structural MRI study of FTLD variants including a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=44) and healthy controls (n=97). The methods use SPM/DARTEL and voxelwise Jacobian-derived change maps warped to MNI space and report group-level voxelwise contrasts (t-maps) between bvFTD and controls with consensus whole-brain change maps and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: (I3) voxelwise morphometric MRI analysis (approach consistent with VBM-type whole-brain voxelwise morphometry), (I4) clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included, (I5) sufficient sample sizes in patient and control groups, (I6) between-group contrasts in standardized (MNI) space comparing bvFTD vs controls (not pooled), (I7) group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented, and (I8) results presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical multicenter study including resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). It enrolled 52 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 60 healthy controls (I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses normalized to MNI space with two-sample t-tests and FWE-corrected results, and presents group-level between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are reported in figures and Supporting Information tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, includes no psychiatric comorbidity pooling, is empirical with original data, and does not rely solely on seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness (E5–E9 not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses resting-state fMRI (alongside other MRI modalities) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=27) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=27; controls n=48) (I5); reports between-group contrasts using standard-space analyses (MNI) comparing bvFTD to controls and to EOAD (voxelwise dual-regression and TBSS analyses) (I6); presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results for the target sample (I7); and these whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplementary materials as described (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary indications) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, seed-only FC/DTI-only/cortical-thickness-only reporting) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This peer-reviewed empirical study (Cortex 2017) reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses in a sample including clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=25) and healthy controls (n=25). The paper includes whole-brain, voxel-wise group comparisons and reports anatomical coordinates (MNI) and cluster results relating atrophy in bvFTD to performance on the TASIT-S. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Imaging modality is VBM. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported and described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate exclusion criteria.

Excluded because imaging methods are surface-based cortical thickness analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, which triggers exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; n=88 patients) and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls; 88 patients, 30 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach — analyses are vertex/surface-based and coordinates/tables in stereotactic space are not provided), and I7 (while whole-brain surface maps are reported, the study does not provide voxelwise whole-brain results in a defined stochastic (MNI/Talairach) space required by the review). Full text appears complete.

This study reports voxel-wise gray matter (GM) density analyses using 3T T1 MRI with Randomise in FSL and reports regression results (peak voxels summarized in table e-1), meeting VBM-style whole-brain analysis reporting in stereotactic space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=32) and matched healthy controls (n=17), both >6. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) and regression associating reduced f0 range with regional GM atrophy. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and patients without concurrent psychiatric/other dementia confounds). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary coordinate table referenced. Therefore all specified inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4) with a healthy control group (n=20) meeting the sample-size requirement (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain two-sample t-tests comparing each patient group (bvFTD and SD) to controls in standard space (MNI) (I6,I7); behavioural VBM correlations are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not restricted to non-qualifying modalities, and no comorbid psychiatric/substance confounds reported). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study meets I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD sample >6 and controls ≥6). However, it does not clearly meet I6 and I7: the paper describes voxelwise FDG-PET comparisons between the overall FTLD group and controls and describes hypometabolic patterns for bvFTD subgroup, but it does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (with results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables/figures) that specifically compares the bvFTD group versus controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. Reported subgroup findings appear descriptive (per-patient or qualitative) and no coordinate-based whole-brain bvFTD>control contrast is provided in the full text supplied. Therefore it fails the requirement for a defined-stochastic-space between-group result for the target sample. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and reports whole-brain voxelwise W-score/atrophy maps comparing bvFTD patients to controls, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=117) and >6 controls, and presents group-level whole-brain results/figures. However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or explicit coordinate tables for between-group contrasts required by criterion I6. Therefore I apply inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I7, and I8, but I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Because the meta-analysis requires reported coordinates for voxelwise between-group contrasts, this paper must be excluded.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T structural MRI and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20 overall; N=17 in MRI analyses) and healthy controls (N=39 overall; N=28 in MRI analyses), exceeding the minimum group sizes. The paper reports VBM atrophy comparisons of bvFTD versus healthy controls and voxelwise correlations of prosocial giving with gray matter volume, including whole-brain follow-up analyses with reported cluster coordinates (e.g., cerebellum coordinates) and clear anatomical localization. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-FC/DTI/cortical thickness only). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical multimodal MRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=20) and matched healthy controls (n=20). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain GM analyses (reported with cluster maxima coordinates) and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6) for both patients and controls. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly reported for the target bvFTD group (text, statistical maps, and coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI-only, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3), enrolled clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (10 patients, 10 controls) to meet I5. However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: (a) bvFTD subjects are pooled with other FTD subtypes in group analyses so there is no between-group contrast that isolates a bvFTD-only group vs controls (I6 not met), and (b) the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) MNI/Talairach result for the bvFTD group (group results are ROI-based and single-subject voxelwise maps are provided) so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the study. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing I6 and I7.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the study reports only linear/region-based measures—Bifrontal Index—without any whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed Frontotemporal Dementia patients using Neary et al. criteria), I5 (patient group size n=23, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; used linear MRI measurements), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls; no control voxelwise comparison reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=13) and healthy controls (N=19), exceeding the minimum group sizes. It reports whole-brain voxelwise structural analyses (VBM using VBM8/DARTEL) and resting-state fMRI analyses (fALFF), satisfying the imaging modality requirement. Group-level between-group contrasts and voxelwise regression results are reported and described with MNI coordinates (e.g., ‘‘Z‐coordinates in MNI space’’) for comparisons involving the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, no comorbid sample issues reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

Although this study meets multiple inclusion requirements (it uses FDG-PET imaging [I3], includes a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample [37 patients, I4], has adequate patient sample size [I5], and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise regression analyses within the bvFTD sample [I7]), it does NOT report a between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper uses patient vs. normative-control database comparisons to define individual hypometabolism and performs regression analyses within the patient group (occupation vs. metabolism), but no group-level bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast in stereotactic coordinates is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses to compare clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=19) to healthy controls (n=20). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and behavioral–neuroimaging correlations with MNI coordinates and cluster results (whole-brain, voxelwise VBM with tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level results. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited imaging modality, and participants without concurrent psychiatric/other dementia conditions). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material availability noted but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study meets all imaging and sample criteria for inclusion. It uses voxel-based morphometry (voxelwise GM density analyses) comparing 63 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) to 55 demographically-matched healthy controls (I3, I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) using nonparametric permutation testing and FWE correction, with results presented as clusters and peak loci converted to Talairach (coordinates reported) (I6, I7, I8). Sample sizes exceed the minimum required. The full text includes methods, results, and figures/tables supporting whole-brain VBM findings. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed modalities or comorbid-sample issues). Therefore the study should be included.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). This paper uses 18F-flortaucipir tau-PET and MR-based FreeSurfer volumetry rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI (resting or task), or FDG-PET required by I3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes: 20 bvFTD, 20 controls), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise comparisons after spatial normalization), and I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modality). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=30) with healthy controls (n=42). Imaging modalities include FDG-PET and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses, and voxelwise diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) results spatially normalized to MNI space. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (ANCOVA/voxel-based DTI and VBM analyses) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls and presents voxel-cluster results (figures/tables) clearly attributed to the target bvFTD sample. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not limited to excluded modalities). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. It is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls (I4, I6, I7). Sample sizes meet the minimum threshold: overall 35 bvFTD and 29 controls, and the VBM subsample included 12 bvFTD and 20 controls (>6) (I5). The VBM processing used MNI152 space and reports cluster results with coordinates referenced in Supplementary Table 3, satisfying the requirement for results in a defined stereotactic space (I6, I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods (including imaging and VBM pipeline), Results (including VBM contrasts and correlations), and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=23; MRI n=21 after QC) (I4). Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD and control groups ≥6; controls: 48 PET, 20 MRI) (I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs BD) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and thresholding details, indicating whole-brain group-level results (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), it presents whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only) (E6), samples do not have excluded comorbidities or substance abuse issues (E7 not met), it is empirical with original data (E8), and it does not exclusively report seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness (E9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=35), uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI, and has adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, the VBM results reported in the main text are correlations of the mind-wandering index within the patient groups combined (bvFTD+AD), not a between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus controls. While the paper references group-level comparisons in the SI Appendix, the provided full text does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast in a standard coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) that isolates the bvFTD group (I6 not met). Likewise, the reported whole-brain VBM results are not clearly identified as originating from the bvFTD group alone (I7 not met). The resting-state findings are seed-based within-group connectivity correlations (not sufficient alone under inclusion rules). Therefore the paper does not meet the required criterion of reporting at least one bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain voxelwise result; it must be excluded.

Excluded because the study uses T1-weighted volumetric segmentation of amygdala subnuclei (ROI-based structural volumetry), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes Pick's disease patients among pathological groups) and I5 (patient and control groups both exceed 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) between-group results comparing bvFTD to controls. This is an rs-fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with adequate sample sizes (41 bvFTD, 39 HC) and extensive network analyses. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients per Rascovsky criteria (I4), has sufficient sample size (25 bvFTD, 20 controls) (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts normalized to MNI space (I6), provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (I7) and presents results in figures/tables/supplementary material (I8). This study is excluded because it does not study clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (it studies asymptomatic MAPT mutation carriers, some of whom later developed MCI or bvFTD features), and it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). This is an empirical VBM study that reports whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates) relating body-composition measures to grey matter atrophy in a separate bvFTD group. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=82) with an HC group (N=82). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all relevant inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (I4); has adequate sample sizes (44/43 patients and 60 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5); and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise VBM results comparing bvFTD to controls (I7) as well as between-group voxelwise contrasts implicit in the VBM analysis (I6). There are concurrent healthy controls (n=110). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text.
